review_notes: I read the whole file and the downstream uses in USTPosteriorResponse.lean. I grepped for uses of finiteTilt and observationField across the repo, and for @[simp] conventions in the SpanningForest directory. The directory uses @[simp] freely for small API lemmas, but this file has none. I did not run Lean, so the findings are about the interface and not about observed simp behaviour. Each suggested simp lemma is a conditional or ground rewrite that cannot loop. I did not flag finiteTilt_empty_eq_zero_field, because its right-hand side contains a variable S that does not occur on the left, so it is unsuitable as a simp lemma. I also did not flag finiteTilt_response (WeightedTreeResponse.lean line 61 declares a theorem of the same name), because that is outside this rubric.

findings.declaration: finiteTilt_of_mem / finiteTilt_of_not_mem (and the downstream uses of `simp only [finiteTilt, dite_eq_right he, ...]`)
findings.excerpt:
lemma finiteTilt_of_not_mem (K : FiniteSubgraphCode) (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ))
    (t : ℝ) (y : (ℕ × ℕ) → ℝ) (e : ℕ × ℕ) (he : e ∉ K.2) :
    finiteTilt K S t y e = 0 := by
  simp [finiteTilt, he]
findings.problem: finiteTilt is a dite on `e ∈ K.2`. The two canonical unfolding lemmas, finiteTilt_of_mem and finiteTilt_of_not_mem, are not tagged @[simp]. Simp therefore has no way to evaluate `finiteTilt K S t y e` when membership is known. Every proof has to unfold the definition by hand: `simp only [finiteTilt, dite_eq_right he, sub_self, abs_zero]` at lines 50, 101 and 117, `simp [finiteTilt, he]` in the two lemmas themselves, and `unfold finiteTilt` at line 63. Downstream, USTPosteriorResponse uses explicit `rw [finiteTilt_of_mem K _ 0 _ e.1 he, ...]`. Unfolding exposes the raw `dite`, which is not the intended normal form. The lemma in the ∉ case already exists, yet the file does not use it in the simp calls at lines 50, 101 and 117.
findings.proposed_change: Mark both lemmas @[simp]. They are conditional rewrites whose side goals `e ∈ K.2` and `e ∉ K.2` are discharged from hypotheses. The right-hand sides do not contain finiteTilt, so there is no loop. Then replace `simp only [finiteTilt, dite_eq_right he, sub_self, abs_zero]` at lines 50, 101 and 117 with `simp only [finiteTilt_of_not_mem K S _ _ e he, sub_self, abs_zero]`, or with a plain `simp [he]`. Do the same for the `dite_eq_left` call at line 48. Keep `finiteTilt` itself unfolded only inside these two lemmas.
findings.benefit: Callers get the canonical forms `inclusion K (observationField ..) ⟨e, he⟩` and `0` from `simp [he]`, with no manual dite unfolding. The proofs stop depending on the internal `dite` representation, so changing the definition of finiteTilt would not break them.

findings.excerpt: fun e => if e.1 ∈ S then y e.1 - t / 2 else 0
findings.problem: observationField has no simp API. There is no `observationField_apply`, and no `_of_mem` / `_of_not_mem` lemmas for `e.1 ∈ S`. Callers unfold the definition and then rewrite the resulting `ite`: lines 99–100 and 115–116 use `simpa only [observationField, ite_eq_left hf, sub_sub_sub_cancel_right]` and `simpa only [observationField, ite_eq_right hf, sub_self, abs_zero]`. Line 123 and line 128 use `simp [observationField]`. USTPosteriorResponse line 40 uses `simp only [observationField, zero_div, sub_zero, indicator]`. The unfolded body `if e.1 ∈ S then y e.1 - t/2 else 0` leaks out and is the only way to evaluate the field. The same `ite` handling is duplicated in finiteTilt_response_of_response and finiteTilt_response.
findings.proposed_change: Add simp lemmas `observationField_of_mem (h : e.1 ∈ S) : observationField K S t y e = y e.1 - t / 2` and `observationField_of_not_mem (h : e.1 ∉ S) : observationField K S t y e = 0`, both tagged @[simp] and both proved by `simp [observationField, h]`. Optionally add `observationField_apply`, kept non-simp, for the ite form. The coordinate-bound steps at lines 99–100 and 115–116 then become `simp [observationField, hf]`-free calls such as `simpa [observationField_of_mem, hf] using hy f.1 hf`. Likewise the `simp only [observationField, ...]` in USTPosteriorResponse can go through these lemmas.
findings.benefit: Simp gets a stable interface instead of an unfolded definition. The two duplicated `by_cases hf` blocks in the response proofs shrink, and later files no longer depend on how observationField is implemented.

findings.excerpt:
lemma observationField_empty (K : FiniteSubgraphCode) (t : ℝ)
    (y : (ℕ × ℕ) → ℝ) : observationField K ∅ t y = 0 := by
findings.problem: These two ground rewrite rules evaluate observationField to `0` when S = ∅ or when t = 0 and y = 0. The target `0` is the canonical form, and the left-hand sides are strictly more complex, so they are natural simp lemmas. They are not tagged @[simp]. Their own proofs and the later use at line 133 go through the `simp [observationField]` unfolding or an explicit `simp only [finiteTilt, observationField_empty, observationField_zero]`. Any other `simp` call that meets `observationField K ∅ t y` or `observationField K S 0 0` must again unfold the definition into an `ite` instead of reaching `0`. Line 138 also needs `rw [..., observationField_zero, ...]` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Mark observationField_zero and observationField_empty @[simp]. There is no loop risk, because the right-hand side `0` is a constant and the rules do not overlap on a non-trivial term. Since y is a function and `0 : (ℕ × ℕ) → ℝ` is a literal, the pattern is syntactically stable. Then finiteTilt_empty_eq_zero_field can be proved by `simp [finiteTilt]`, and the `rw` at lines 138–139 can be dropped in favour of `simp`.
findings.benefit: The degenerate cases (no observed edges, and zero time with zero data) normalize to the zero field automatically. Users reasoning about the unobserved or zero-tilt case do not have to remember these lemma names or unfold observationField.
